title: The published Gaia20cdd continuum limits cool thermal band sources but permits a tested hot source mixture
abstract: We test whether a separate thermal source can make the reported 3.1 um band of Gaia20cdd. A linear program fits a free stellar scale and positive thermal mixtures to the published SPHEREx continuum. For temperatures at most 650 K and emissivity exponents 0, 1 or 2, the tested three-error boxes permit at most 12.5 percent thermal light at 3.1 um. Even a generous stellar band bound then gives total depth at most 0.240, below the reported central depth 0.33. Hot mixtures give a different result. A beta 2 mixture near 680 K and 2000 K supplies 40 percent thermal light and fits all 26 continuum bins within two errors. Absorption of 82.5 percent of that component would give depth 0.33 without a stellar band. This is continuum feasibility, not a physical ice-cloud solution. Smooth extinction, material emissivity, geometry and energy balance are not linked in this model. Error boxes are not confidence regions, the spectrum averages visits, and thermal bounds use finite grids. Code, source hashes, coefficients and grid checks are supplied.

display.caption: Limits from the published continuum and an allowed hot mixture. Error boxes are sensitivity sets, not confidence regions.
